latest.title: Real-World AWS Architecture: Deploying a Secure E-Commerce Application
latest.description:
Imagine a growing e-commerce company that wants to move its online shopping platform to AWS.

Initially, the application runs on a single server. As customer traffic increases, the company starts experiencing slow response times, security concerns, and downtime.

The challenge is to build an architecture that can handle increasing traffic while keeping customer data secure.

Let's see how AWS can solve this problem.

latest.title: Your AI Agent Has AWS Access. What Happens If Someone Hacks It?
latest.description: What happens when an AI agent with AWS permissions encounters a malicious prompt or attempts an unauthorized action? Explore the security risks of AI agents, , excessive IAM permissions, unauthorized tool execution, and sensitive data exposure. Learn how Amazon Bedrock Guardrails,  Lambda, application-level authorization, human approval,  can help build more secure AI-powered cloud applications. Includes a practical architecture, illustrative Python example, security checklist, and AWS references.

latest.title: Route Easy Questions to a Cheaper Model: A Cost-Aware LLM Router on Amazon Bedrock
latest.description: Build a small-model router and prompt caching for a chatbot, then prove with your own numbers whether they save money without making the answers worse. Deploy, verify, and clean up included.

latest.title: Automating Image Upload and Processing Using AWS Cloud Services
latest.description: This project demonstrates how to automate image uploading and processing using AWS cloud services. Images uploaded to Amazon S3 can trigger AWS Lambda functions to perform automated processing tasks such as resizing, format conversion, and image organization. The project highlights event-driven architecture, serverless computing, and cloud automation while providing a scalable solution for managing digital images.

latest.title: The Agent Is Just Another Client: Safe Database Writes with Strands Agents on AWS
latest.description: Learn how a chat agent can add plants and log actions in DynamoDB through the same validated code as your REST endpoints, with user and garden IDs that the model can never supply or change.

latest.title: Understanding CI/CD Pipelines: A Practical Guide to Continuous Integration and Deployment on AWS
latest.description: Learn how modern engineering teams ship features faster and safer by automating code building, testing, and release workflows. Explore the core stages of an automated release pipeline and discover how AWS Developer Tools and GitHub Actions power reliable cloud deployments.

latest.title: How to Design a Scalable Backend for a Multi-Tenant SaaS Application on AWS
latest.description: Designing a scalable multi-tenant SaaS backend on AWS is really about managing boundaries—between tenants, data, permissions, services, and failure domains. This guide covers the key architectural decisions: defining a tenant model, enforcing tenant-aware authorization, choosing compute, isolating data and caches, handling noisy neighbors, adding async processing, building tenant-aware observability, and planning for failure—without over-engineering version one.

latest.title: Day 3: AWS Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) – Configuring, Scaling, and Monitoring Instances
latest.description: Day 3 of my AWS learning journey! Today, I'm exploring Amazon EC2, understanding instance types, configuring security groups and key pairs, and learning how to scale and monitor cloud servers using EC2 Auto Scaling and Amazon CloudWatch. This article also includes practical AWS CLI commands and hands-on learning activities.
